translation_notes: Five one-step traversals (graph.objects(entity_uri, PRED)) become five m{ {s} pred ?o } reads, each arity 1 (a single named variable), matching the stratum's target exactly. The nested for p in graph.objects(entity_uri, parent_pred) uses a dynamically chosen predicate (rdfs:subPropertyOf or rdfs:subClassOf depending on entity_type), interpolated as {parent_pred} in predicate position -- a plain Python variable holding a URIRef term, same treatment as a subject/object interpolation.

@graph graph designates the function's own graph parameter as current for the whole body, so every m{ } stays bare (no (graph) call suffix needed) -- matches current-graph.md's 'designate the existing Python variable as current' form.

_local_name (called for the primary label and for a parent with no rdfs:label of its own) is not defined in the extracted region: it is a private helper further down in the same source file (ontokit/services/embedding_text_builder.py, lines 56-60 at commit 23680a4d04). Restored via a context shim (embedding_text_context.py), reproduced verbatim from the published source, imported identically by both original.py and translated.ldpy.

isinstance(o, RDFLiteral) after each m{ } read is preserved as-is: it is ordinary Python filtering a term island already returns (a URIRef, Literal or BNode), not something m{ } itself needs to express -- the fixture's non-literal rdfs:label object on ex:Animal exercises this filter on both sides.

fixture calls exercise: (1) ex:Animal/class -- two labels (labels[1:] extra-label path), comment-over-definition priority, one owl:Thing parent dropped and one kept parent with its own label, one alt label, and a non-literal rdfs:label object dropped by the isinstance filter; (2) ex:WorksAt/property -- the subPropertyOf branch and the 'no comment, fall back to definition' branch; (3) ex:Empty/class -- the zero-solution case across every field (label, comment/definition, parents, alt labels all empty), falling back to _local_name.

Correction du 2026-10-31 (audit par mutation) : `@graph graph` liait les `@prefix owl:/rdfs:/skos:` du bloc dans le graphe de l'appelant, que le dépôt a parsé depuis le fichier d'ontologie du projet, met en cache (ontology.py load_from_git/load_from_storage) puis resert (OntologyService.serialize, linter.py lit graph.namespaces()) : un fichier qui nomme SKOS `sk:` ou OWL `ow:` voyait ces préfixes renommés en `skos:`/`owl:`. Preuve : sur fixture_prefixes.ttl le pilote renforcé rend FAIL pour l'ancienne traduction (('ow', OWL) et ('sk', SKOS) disparaissent). Corrigé en retirant `@graph graph` et en suffixant chaque `m{ }` de `(graph)`, qui ne lie rien ; `constructions` suit (@graph -> call suffix (g)).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the five copies of `[str(o) for o in graph.objects(s, P) if isinstance(o, RDFLiteral)]` become one local helper literals(subject, predicate); comments/definitions become `desc = literals(.., RDFS.comment) or literals(.., SKOS.definition)`; the parent loop becomes a list comprehension with `next(iter(literals(p, RDFS.label)), _local_name(str(p)))` (default still evaluated eagerly, as in the original); parts starts as `[f"{entity_type}: {primary_label}"]`; alt_labels and extra_labels are folded into all_alt. All section comments and the docstring are kept.

optimized.ldpy is optimized.py with the helper's read and the parent read as `m{ {subject} {predicate} ?o }(graph)` / `m{ {entity_uri} {parent_pred} ?p }(graph)` and the namespace terms as prefixed names. No @graph: the call suffix (graph) binds nothing in the caller's graph (2026-10-31 correction of the translation), and with only two islands left it costs no more than a designation.
No exception to symmetry. The helper absorbs most of what the notation would have saved: once the five reads share one line, the notation has a single read to rewrite, hence a notation ratio near 1.
